text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Employers' association Federmeccanica rejected as "unacceptable" a proposal put forward by the government which included a 200,000 lire monthly pay rise for metalworkers to end a long-running dispute. Labour minister Tiziano Treu said he would restart talks "at the very beginning of January" (all).

* PDS party leader Massimo D'Alema, commenting on Federmeccanica's refusal, says "it is a serious decision, they want to make life impossible for the government", while trade union leader Sergio Cofferati does not rule out calling a general strike (all).
* From leftist PDS to far-right National Alliance, party leaders reject the idea of a broad government coalition suggested by opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi (all).

* Insurance company INA said it would buy BNL Vita from Banca Nazionale del lavoro and would also cede control of INA Banca to BNL. The moves are part of a joint effort to bid for a 60 percent stake in ailing Banco di Napoli. In an interview with French newspaper Les Echos, Prime minister Romano Prodi reportedly said INA would be the core shareholder in the new banking group.
Prodi also told Les Echos extra budget measures, if needed, would not exceed 14 trillion lire (all).

* The government is expected to announce on December 30 the details of a maxi-decree to bring in 4.3 trillion lire by raising taxes on petrol, cigarettes, mobile phones and the national lottery. The measure is included in the 1997 budget approved by parliament over the weekend (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
